title: The Faithful Regiment
premise: Edmund Okonkwo, an apprentice clockmaker hiding her identity as a woman behind her late brother's name, is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock in a port city ruled by a garrison that calls itself the Faithful Regiment. While inside, she uncovers ledgers proving the Regiment has been selling conscripted men to a slaving syndicate, and when census taker Miriam Halloway notices the discrepancies in her papers, the two form an uneasy alliance. To bring the evidence to a reformist magistrate aboard a departing ship, Edmund must smuggle the ledgers past three checkpoints before the morning tide, risking the exposure she has spent years avoiding. She succeeds at devastating cost: her mentor dies covering her escape, the Regiment falls, and Edmund, choosing to live openly at last, sails not to flee but to testify.
about_author: U. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent a decade restoring maritime instruments before turning to fiction. Sterling writes historical novels about people whose careful, invisible work keeps the world running.

chapters.title: The Escapement
chapters.summary: Edmund Okonkwo, a woman passing as her dead brother, repairs clocks in a cramped port-city shop and keeps her hands too busy to be noticed. POV: Edmund. Beat: quiet tension, the cost of invisibility established.

chapters.title: Summons from the Tower
chapters.summary: A Regiment officer orders Edmund to repair the observatory's master clock, which has stopped for the first time in forty years. Her mentor, old Vasco, warns her that the tower sees everything. POV: Edmund. Beat: dread beneath obligation.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Census taker Miriam Halloway arrives at the shop with her ledger of names and asks why Edmund's handwriting appears on documents dated before her brother's death. POV: Miriam. Beat: the trap closes gently.

chapters.title: The Stopped Clock
chapters.summary: Inside the observatory, Edmund finds the master clock deliberately jammed and hidden ledgers recording conscripts sold to a slaving syndicate. POV: Edmund. Beat: horror disguised as discovery.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Vestry
chapters.summary: Edmund confronts Miriam; rather than expose her, Miriam reveals her own brother was conscripted and vanished. They agree to trust each other. POV: alternating. Beat: wary alliance, first warmth.

chapters.title: The Regiment at Prayer
chapters.summary: Edmund observes the garrison's public ceremony and recognizes Colonel Ashworth's private secretary among the men listed as 'sold' in the ledgers. POV: Edmund. Beat: the enemy gains a face.

chapters.title: What Vasco Knew
chapters.summary: Vasco admits he helped build the observatory's clock as a records vault decades ago and suspected the Regiment's rot but stayed silent. He gives Edmund a key. POV: Vasco. Beat: guilt passed down like an heirloom.

chapters.title: The Census Ledger
chapters.summary: Miriam cross-references census records with the hidden ledgers, finding forty-one missing men, and realizes her own superiors are complicit. POV: Miriam. Beat: disillusionment hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Harbor Gate
chapters.summary: A first test: Edmund smuggles copied pages sewn into a clock case through the harbor gate, nearly undone by a soldier who knew her brother. POV: Edmund. Beat: terror, narrow success.

chapters.title: The Ship on the Morning Tide
chapters.summary: They learn the reformist magistrate Corvane sails in nine days and will accept evidence against the Regiment. Nine days, three checkpoints. POV: Miriam. Beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Ashworth's Dinner
chapters.summary: Colonel Ashworth invites Edmund to dine, praising her craftsmanship, and mentions the master clock's 'irregularities' with a smile. POV: Edmund. Beat: the predator circling, politeness as menace.

chapters.title: A Room with Two Doors
chapters.summary: Edmund and Miriam hide the originals in Miriam's census office and admit, almost accidentally, that their bond has become more than strategy. POV: Miriam. Beat: love against duty named aloud.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Customs House
chapters.summary: A customs officer detains the clock case; Miriam forges a census seal to free it, burning her official career in the process. POV: alternating. Beat: sacrifice, deepening trust.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: A fellow apprentice, jealous and frightened, reports 'irregularities' about Edmund to the Regiment. Ashworth orders her watched. POV: Edmund. Beat: the walls closing in.

chapters.title: Vasco's Confession
chapters.summary: Vasco offers himself as decoy, planning to confess his old silence publicly to draw the Regiment's eyes. Edmund begs him not to. POV: Vasco. Beat: an old man choosing redemption over safety.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Regiment Barracks
chapters.summary: The final checkpoint lies through the barracks yard; Edmund repairs Ashworth's own chronometer as cover, hands steady while everything trembles. POV: Edmund. Beat: courage as craft.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Tide
chapters.summary: Ashworth's men raid the census office; Miriam is taken. Edmund must choose: flee with the evidence or go back for her. POV: Edmund. Beat: the heart over the mission.

chapters.title: The Clock Strikes True
chapters.summary: Vasco triggers the master clock's restored chimes as a signal and is arrested in the square; his sacrifice clears Edmund's path to the cells. POV: Vasco. Beat: grief as fuel.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Regiment
chapters.summary: Edmund frees Miriam during the chaos of Vasco's public confession, and the two run for the docks as alarms rise. POV: alternating. Beat: climax, breathless flight.

chapters.title: Corvane's Cabin
chapters.summary: Aboard the ship, Edmund delivers the ledgers to Magistrate Corvane and, for the first time in years, speaks her own name aloud. POV: Edmund. Beat: identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Fall of Ashworth
chapters.summary: Word arrives as the ship weighs anchor: Ashworth arrested, the syndicate exposed, Vasco awaiting trial as a witness, not a criminal. POV: Miriam. Beat: justice outside the law, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Faithful
chapters.summary: Edmund and Miriam sail together toward the trial, Edmund keeping her brother's name and adding her own beneath it. POV: Edmund. Beat: belonging chosen, not granted; a quiet, open ending.
